summary: Pause-resume race causes half-formed markdown closing bracket and missing image URL on resumed SSE sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDesk reports that long SSE streams which contain markdown with image embeds intermittently resume with the final closing bracket of a code block or image markdown truncated (e.g. '![screenshot](https://.../img.png' with missing ')'). The result is a half-formed markdown block and the image URL is not recognized by their renderer. The problem appears only after a short pause in the connection (~3-7s) followed by an automatic resume. Impact:
- End users see broken markdown or missing images for a small percentage (~1.2%) of long streaming responses.
- Customer has a production job that relies on rendered transcripts; this causes visual corruption and downstream parsing failures.
Environment:
- prod (us-east) behind customer's corporate edge proxy and ALB.
- Requests via browser-based SDK and server-to-server SDK.
Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1) Use BrightDesk test workload (large narratives + base64 image references) against redwood-open-7b-v2.
2) Simulate a 3-7s network pause (client backgrounding or proxy backoff), then allow socket to resume.
3) Observe resumed SSE stream in browser: trailing markdown closing token or final ')' of image URL missing; sometimes final '
```' removed.
Logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Customer-provided HAR and tcpdump snippets attached to the ticket (see comments).
- Sample truncated stream payload (sanitized) included in comments.
Additional notes:
- Customer reports increase after they rotated their corporate proxy to introduce HTTP/2 connection coalescing ~2 weeks ago.
- Affects both SSE and long-lived WebSocket-to-SSE fallback sessions.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Marta Novak (Support): Acknowledged report. Requested HAR, raw payload and region. Asked customer to reproduce with SDK verbose logging enabled.

2026-03-10 - BrightDesk (Customer): Uploaded sanitized tcpdump and HAR. Customer notes issue spikes when their ALB drains connections for short periods. They've observed truncated final ')' on image markdown in ~1.2% of resumed sessions.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen (SRE): Initial triage: replicated pause-resume locally using a test proxy. Observed stream resume where final 1-16 bytes missing when proxy performs a stream pause and resumes underlying TCP channel. Repro appears correlated with proxy-level HTTP/2 flow control and chunk coalescing.

2026-03-11 - Eng (runtime): Added trace log of SSE framing and noticed final '\n' delimiter not flushed in some codepaths when session resumes during edge backpressure. Pushing instrumented build to staging for additional repros.
2026-03-11 - BrightDesk (Customer): Verified that sending a short keepalive every 2s reduces occurrence. They cannot disable ALB settings due to internal policy.

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen (SRE): Temporary workaround provided: patch the SDK to insert an explicit terminal sentinel (<END_OF_STREAM>) when resuming and recommend BrightDesk upgrade SDK. Advised customer to route traffic via our regional private link as a short-term mitigation.
2026-03-12 - Marta Novak (Support): Notified customer of planned server-side fix and ETA. Marked ticket In Progress and escalated to serving-runtime owners.
2026-03-12 - Eng (runtime): Confirmed PR created to ensure final-frame flush and to add resilience to partial-chunk reassembly under HTTP/2 window adjustments. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4951
investigation_notes: Instrumented staging to reproduce: introduced artificial 4s stall in upstream read path; observed identical truncated trailing tokens in 9/100 runs.
Hypothesis: edge-proxy HTTP/2 flow control + ALB idle-probe creates a pause where the runtime's chunk-assembler returns early and final flush of the terminal delimiter is lost during socket rebind.
Correlated traces: client-seq 1023 shows last bytes not ACKed before pause; resumed TCP shows new stream id and payload missing last 10-14 bytes. No 5xx returned by runtime.
SDK behaviour: older SDKs do reliant optimistic buffering which assumes the server will always send terminal delimiter; adding a client sentinel reduces failed renders.
Related historical tickets: some overlap with SUP-314271 (resume delta issues) but this case includes image-URL-specific missing ')', likely due to being at chunk boundary during pause.
Risk: medium — data loss limited to final bytes of streams on resume scenarios, not entire conversations. However customer's parsing pipeline is sensitive to exact markdown closure.
resolution: Short-term workaround (customer action): upgrade to patched SDK v2.3.1 which emits explicit resume sentinel and performs local reassembly checks; route critical jobs over private link to avoid ALB-induced pauses.

Immediate mitigation (platform): increased server-side final-frame flush retries in staging and added a verification that final delimiter was sent before connection handoff (hotfix branch: github.com/redwood/repo/commit/9a7b2f1).

Planned permanent fix: adjust serving-runtime chunk-assembler to hold final-terminal bytes until end-of-session confirmation, add idempotent sequence numbering for streamed frames, and add regression tests simulating HTTP/2 pause/resume and ALB probe churn. Target rollout: canary 2026-03-18, global rollout 2026-03-23.
Follow-up actions: create postmortem and add to streaming-resume-runbook. Coordinate with partner/EDGE team to publish guidance for customers behind aggressive ALB/HTTP/2 coalescing proxies.
Status: workaround accepted by customer; server-side hotfix validated in staging. ETA for canary: 2026-03-18.
